payload.name: Verify Event Coverage Before SKIP
payload.description: Use during CRUD decisions before skipping an event candidate as already represented; check whether the existing memory covers the specific event details, not just a related theme.
content: During CRUD, before SKIPping a candidate as already represented, compare against the matched memory's specific facts: subject, action, object, and time. A general trait, impact, or preference statement does not cover a specific event.

If the existing memory only overlaps thematically (e.g., a writing-impact profile vs. a received-letter event), do not SKIP; ADD a new event memory or MERGE only if the event details are already present.
Check the full existing memory content for the event's distinguishing facts; do not assume an enrichment update will later add them, because it may not.

solves: Construction decisions sometimes skip a correctly extracted event because a related profile or preference memory seems to cover the same theme, losing the specific event and its timing. This guides CRUD to require event-specific facts before skipping.
